seoDescription: Learn to set up a powerful local AI server using vLLM in a Proxmox LXC container with GPU passthrough. This guide walks you through restoring a container from a backup, configuring network settings, and allocating storage. You'll install vLLM and its dependencies like Flash Attention using Python's pipenv. Discover how to launch an AI model server for models like JanV14B from Hugging Face and connect it to your Open Web UI instance alongside Ollama and Llama C++, creating a robust and flexible home lab setup.

chapters.description: This chapter breaks down the command used to start the vLLM API server, explaining each parameter and showing the process of downloading the model from Hugging Face.

chapters.description: Walk through the process of connecting the newly created vLLM server as a backend in Open Web UI and testing the model through the chat interface.

chapters.description: This chapter summarizes the setup process, demonstrates creating a Proxmox snapshot for easy rollbacks, and concludes the guide series.

summary:
## Overview
This guide demonstrates how to set up **vLLM** in a **Proxmox LXC container** with **GPU passthrough**, building on previous tutorials for Ollama and Llama.cpp. The objective is to create a powerful, flexible, and easily manageable local AI server environment.

## LXC Container Setup
- **Restoration**: The process begins by restoring a pre-configured LXC container backup from the previous Llama C++ guide.
- **Configuration Updates**:
  - **Networking**: The static IP address is changed (e.g., from `.71` to `.72`) to avoid conflicts with other containers.
  - **Storage**: The root disk is resized to accommodate large model files. An additional `20 GB` is added in the video's example.
> [!IMPORTANT]
> Do not overallocate storage. It is one of the most common constraints in home lab setups, second only to RAM.

## vLLM Installation
- **Environment**: A Python environment is created using **pipenv**, a simple environment manager.
  - `sudo apt update && sudo apt install python3-pip -y`
  - `pip install pipenv`
- **Core Dependencies**: The vLLM installation command includes several key packages to enable high-performance inference.
  - `pipenv install vllm flash-attn transformers flash-infer`

> [!TIP]
> This installation process can take a significant amount of time to complete.

## Launching the Model Server
- The vLLM server is started via the command line, which exposes an OpenAI-compatible API endpoint.
- **Example Command Parameters**:
  - `python -m vllm.entrypoints.openai.api_server`: The main command to start the server.
  - `--model Jan-v1.4b`: Specifies the model to serve from Hugging Face.
  - `--max-model-len 32768`: Sets the maximum context length.
  - `--api-key nerdtastic`: Secures the API endpoint with a secret key.
  - `--port 42069`: Designates the listening port.
  - `--host 0.0.0.0`: Allows network access from any IP.
  - `--tensor-parallel-size 4`: Distributes the model across 4 GPUs for parallel processing.

> [!NOTE]
> On its first run, vLLM will automatically download the specified model from Hugging Face if it is not present in the local cache.

## Connecting to Open Web UI
- vLLM can be integrated as a backend service for chat frontends like **Open Web UI**.
- **Connection Steps**:
  1. In Open Web UI, navigate to **Settings > Admin Settings > Connections**.
  2. Define a **Prefix ID** (e.g., `vllm-`) to easily identify models from this vLLM instance.
  3. Enter the **API Base URL**: `http://<LXC-IP-ADDRESS>:<PORT>/v1`.
  4. Provide the **API Key** that you defined when launching the server.
  5. Verify the connection and save. The system can now serve models from Ollama, Llama.cpp, and vLLM through a single interface.

## System Management
- **Backups**: After completing the setup, it is crucial to take a **snapshot** of the LXC container in Proxmox.
- This creates a reliable, known-good restore point, making it simple to recover from any future misconfigurations or failed experiments.
